title: Should we adopt axioms that decide CH

problemStatement.formal: \text{The Continuum Hypothesis is independent of ZFC. Should we adopt additional axioms that settle CH, and if so, which ones?}
problemStatement.plain: The Continuum Hypothesis (CH) states 2^ℵ₀ = ℵ₁. Gödel (1940) and Cohen (1963) showed CH is independent of ZFC. The open question is: are there natural, well-motivated axioms we should add to ZFC that would settle CH? The question has two directions: axioms implying CH (V=L, Ultimate L) and axioms implying ¬CH (PFA, MM). A key asymmetry: CH-implying axioms like V=L are incompatible with large cardinal axioms (Scott 1961), while ¬CH-implying axioms like PFA are compatible.
whyMatters: Foundation of all mathematics: ZFC's incompleteness means we must decide what axioms to use
Large cardinal theory: incompatibility of V=L with measurable cardinals forces a choice
Forcing axioms (PFA, MM) have rich mathematical consequences beyond CH
Woodin's Ultimate L program seeks to simultaneously accommodate GCH and large cardinals

proven: CH is independent of ZFC (Gödel 1940, Cohen 1963)
V=L is incompatible with measurable cardinals (Scott 1961)
PFA implies 2^ℵ₀ = ℵ₂, hence ¬CH (Foreman, Magidor, Shelah 1988)
ℵ₁ ≤ 2^ℵ₀ is provable in ZFC alone (Cantor + ordinal successor)
open: Ultimate L conjecture (Woodin): does a canonical inner model satisfying GCH and all large cardinals exist?
Which (if any) CH-deciding axiom is the 'correct' extension of ZFC?
Are there natural CH-deciding axioms beyond V=L, PFA, and MM?
